item.title: Manhattan College Avenue UMC Partners with KMF - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: College Avenue United Methodist Church in Manhattan is one of may churches that partners with the Kansas Methodist Foundation to manage investments and ensure the church has a bright financial future. As a financial steward independent of church membership, KMF adds value as the church grows resources in a way that reflects United Methodist values.

item.title: Barlow-Thompson Family Speaks on How Estate Planning Impacted Them - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: Ashley Prescott Barlow-Thompson and Adam Barlow-Thompson both serve in ministries in the Wichita area. They are one of hundreds of families who have benefited from partnering with the Kansas Methodist Foundation to plan their estate, provide for their family, and support the charitable causes they value most.

item.title: Taking a Next Step in Generosity - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: How do you take a next step to grow your generosity and your faith? For many, it comes from a vision for making a difference with the resources entrusted to us. It also takes a love of neighbor and stepping out in faith because of God’s generosity and grace. Bret and Laura Henderson and their three children are actively involved in College Avenue United Methodist Church in Manhattan, KS. In 2024, they took a next step in growing their generosity to make a difference.

item.title: Faith, Family, and Forward Thinking - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: Phil and Carol Mattox are both natives of Georgia and attended rival high schools outside Atlanta. They met on a blind date arranged by common friends. Fast forward 54 years later, they now have two children and six grandchildren.

item.title: For Everything a Season - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: The poetry of Ecclesiastes in Chapter 3 speaks of a shared experience in life: things come into being, serve a purpose, and then an ending happens. There is “a time to be born and a time to die” (3:2). This is the case for our human lives. This is the case for projects we work to advance. This is the case even for the life of congregations.

item.title: 2024 Annual Report - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: In 2024, KMF continued growing our ministry with Methodist families, churches, and organizations. We are called into this unique ministry of stewardship and generosity so that together we make a lasting difference in the name of Jesus Christ. Thank you for joining us on this shared journey.

item.title: Now Hiring - Development Coach - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: The Kansas Methodist Foundation is currently seeking a KC Area Development Coach to join our team.

item.title: Rachel Hixson Named Communications Associate - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: Rachel joined our team in September 2025 as our Communications Associate. She will manage our communications and marketing efforts while also helping to run our office. We’re excited to bring her aboard!

item.title: Charitable Giving and the One Big Beautiful Bill: What’s Changing in 2026? - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: The One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB) Act has reshaped the tax landscape for charitable giving, changing what donors can expect starting in 2026. While people don’t give only for tax reasons, tax incentives still matter — and they often influence how much people give and when they choose to give. Join us for this webinar to explore what’s changing, how the new law affects charitable giving, and what the updated tax implications mean for you and members of your congregation.

item.title: Susan Brinkman to Lead New Kansas City Development Coach program - Kansas Methodist Foundation
item.description: We’re excited to welcome Susan Brinkman as our new Kansas City Development Coach. With decades of leadership and fundraising experience, she’ll support churches and ministries across the KC area, focusing on long-term growth and giving.
